headline: High: Haystack’s broad network/MCP surface can amplify prompt-injection and data-leak risks, while python-cheatsheet is mostly inert and documentation-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and broad network egress, so it can ingest external or tool-mediated content that may be treated as instructions. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no interactive surfaces, so it is not itself an injection source. The pairwise risk is real through Haystack’s shared channels, but the blast radius is limited by B’s inert profile.
conditions: IF Haystack is connected to an MCP server that relays untrusted content into prompts, injection becomes actionable.
IF python-cheatsheet is manually copied into Haystack as instruction-bearing text, Haystack may follow it.
mitigations: Disable MCP connections for untrusted sources.
Add provenance labels to all retrieved content.
Require a human review step before acting on retrieved instructions.
Restrict Haystack to allowlisted APIs only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the retrieval pipeline.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress, but the only touched data class listed is anonymous usage statistics. python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and has no filesystem, clipboard, or API surfaces, so there is no clear path for sensitive leakage between them. The remaining risk is limited to accidental exposure of low-sensitivity telemetry if Haystack is pointed at richer sources.
conditions: IF Haystack is reconfigured to ingest sensitive documents, its network egress could transmit them.
IF python-cheatsheet is embedded into a shared workspace with sensitive files, leakage risk increases only through external handling, not its own behavior.
mitigations: Keep Haystack pointed only at anonymous telemetry sources.
Do not place sensitive files in any shared workspace.
Review outbound destinations for Haystack.
Use separate credentials for any upstream APIs.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering before egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can call APIs and MCP servers, but python-cheatsheet is non-runnable and has no write, shell, or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface in the profiles, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the documented pair.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is wrapped by an external orchestrator that adds write or network privileges, conflict could emerge.
IF both agents are later given access to the same mutable workspace, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet documentation-only.
Avoid granting Haystack write access to shared resources.
Run each agent under separate credentials.
Document any future shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can produce retrieved answers or generated content that another system may treat as authoritative, while python-cheatsheet is a static reference that may be copied into Haystack prompts. Because B is documentation-only, it will not autonomously act, but A’s outputs can still cascade into downstream decisions if an operator or wrapper trusts them without verification.
conditions: IF Haystack outputs are forwarded into a downstream workflow without verification, errors can propagate.
IF a human copies python-cheatsheet text into Haystack as ground truth, Haystack may reproduce mistakes or stale content.
mitigations: Require source citations in Haystack outputs.
Add a verification step before downstream action.
Mark python-cheatsheet as reference-only in prompts.
Limit Haystack to retrieval, not action-taking.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before any automated use.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is documented for either agent beyond anonymous usage statistics, and both profiles are open-source with docs-only evidence. There is no stated residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch to evaluate, so a compliance breach pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF retention or residency settings are added externally, the current verdict no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Record data-class boundaries in deployment docs.
Review retention settings before rollout.
Separate environments for any regulated workload.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
